text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: unusual egress pattern from edge-proxy cluster in us-west-2. Alert ID: ALERT-4521. High request volume to external s3 endpoints matching log-push patterns.
Tim Khanna: oncall here, pulling up traces. Any immediate customer impact?
Alice Nguyen: seeing repeated HEAD/PUT to s3://redwood-staging-logs from svc-account edge-ingress-01 starting ~04:12 UTC. Volumes small but sustained.
Ben Park: confirmed — pattern looks like automated push, not standard logshipper id. IPs: 18.205.3.14, 52.20.122.9.
Carol Li: is this our log-forwarder or an unknown agent? Could be staging creds leaked.
Tim Khanna: @Alice can you paste the minimal log sample?
Alice Nguyen: here, quick snippet from proxy logs:
```
[04:13:02] edge-proxy-03 PUT /logs/2026-01-18/edge.log 200 svc=svc-edge-ingress-01 auth=SvcToken abbr=push size=2.1KB src=18.205.3.14
[04:13:12] edge-proxy-03 PUT /logs/2026-01-18/edge.log 200 svc=svc-edge-ingress-01 auth=SvcToken abbr=push size=2.0KB src=52.20.122.9
[04:13:22] edge-proxy-03 PUT /logs/2026-01-18/edge.log 200 svc=svc-edge-ingress-01 auth=SvcToken abbr=push size=2.3KB src=18.205.3.14
```
Tim Khanna: thanks. That svc-account should only write to internal-logs S3, not staging buckets. Marking this as potential misconfigured key or exfil.
Dave O'Connor: starting immediate key rotation for svc-edge-ingress-01. I'll create a short-lived replacement and revoke old creds. ETA 7m.
Erin Morales: notifying Support and Legal: possible customer-identifiable logs in staging bucket. Support: hold off sending user-facing comms until we confirm scope. Legal: please standby for potential data exposure assessment.
Ben Park: adding firewall rule to block the two IPs at the edge layer as temporary mitigation. Applying now.
Carol Li: also enabling audit mode on S3 bucket so we have full object-level access logs (if not already).
Tim Khanna: great. Next steps: 1) rotate svc-account keys (Dave) 2) block IPs + rate-limit (Ben) 3) confirm destination objects and owners (Alice/Carol) 4) notify affected customers if PII present (Erin/Legal) 5) run scope query for last 24h (me).
Dave O'Connor: rotated keys, created new creds with reduced write scope, revoked old token, pushed change to kube secret for logshipper. Old token revoked at 04:19 UTC.
Incident Bot: Deployment event: secret-update edge/logshipper - success (deployed by dave.oconnor).
Alice Nguyen: scanning bucket now for object creators with svc-edge-ingress-01 and timestamp >= 04:00 UTC. Initial result: 48 objects, mostly compressed edge logs. Sampling first 3 — no obvious customer PII in headers, but still performing deeper grep.
Ben Park: IP blocks applied, traffic drop observed. Rate down from ~1200 PUT/min to <10.
Erin Morales: Legal looking at whether logs contain email/identifiers and will advise on disclosure. Support prepping draft non-technical note in case we need to contact customers.
Carol Li: suggest enforcing stricter IAM: deny PutObject to external buckets for any staging svc-accounts and add automated guardrail.
Tim Khanna: agree. Post-mortem action item: create guardrail + augment CI secret-scanning for staging creds.
Dave O'Connor: will open rotation/rbac PR and link in this thread.
Alice Nguyen: scan complete: 48 objects, 0 matches for email regex in indexed fields, but will run parser for tokens.
Erin Morales: legal: likely not a widespread PII exposure based on initial scan, proceeding with internal notification only. If anything definitive changes, we'll escalate.
Tim Khanna: closing urgent mitigation: keys rotated, IPs blocked, rate normalized. Keeping thread open for next 24h for follow-up and post-mortem notes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
